## Deck Goal
Explain speculative decoding to a general English-class audience in an 8-minute group presentation, with four speakers sharing the talk equally.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "Based mainly on Hugging Face's article about assisted generation, with the original speculative decoding paper used for credibility. The core mechanism is simple: a smaller draft model proposes several tokens quickly, and the larger target model verifies them, accepting correct guesses and replacing the first wrong guess.",
    "core_claim": "Speculative decoding speeds up text generation by letting a fast helper model draft tokens while the large model still controls the final output.",
    "canonical_terms": [
      "speculative decoding",
      "assisted generation",
      "draft model",
      "target model",
      "token",
      "verification",
      "accepted token",
      "rejected token"
    ],
    "speaker_split": "Speaker 1 covers slides 1-3, Speaker 2 covers slides 4-6, Speaker 3 covers slides 7-9, and Speaker 4 covers slides 10-12."
  }
}
